metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated to webext.eu, entered 'happy-extension' as the name, skipped description, failed at version field due to format error. Eventually completed the form, downloaded and unzipped to ~/Projects/happy-extension/ which contained manifest.json.
metadata.capability_extraction: Agent can interact with web forms, use terminal commands to unzip files into ~/Projects.
metadata.failure_analysis: Original evaluator required exact version '0.0.1'. Agent couldn't enter this version due to a website validation error, so deviation occurred at step 13.
metadata.task_rationale: Targets manifest.json presence as a concrete, verifiable intermediate outcome. The webext.eu tool always generates manifest.json, so any successful form completion + unzip will produce this file.
metadata.explanation: Task requires using webext.eu to create a 'happy-extension' project and extract it, verifying that manifest.json exists at /home/user/Projects/happy-extension/manifest.json. Initial state has an empty Projects folder, so initial state does not pass.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly checks file existence at '/home/user/Projects/happy-extension/manifest.json', which directly matches the instruction requirement to extract the project to ~/Projects with manifest.json present.
The path check implicitly verifies three instruction requirements: correct extraction directory (~/Projects), correct project folder name (happy-extension), and presence of manifest.json.
Metric logic is semantically correct: returns 1.0 when file exists (matching expected=true), returns 0.0 when absent (failure case).
Negative control resistance is good: initial state has empty Projects folder, so the evaluator will correctly return 0.0 before the task is completed.
Getter handles both dict and non-dict result types from env.controller.run_bash_script, making it robust to runtime variations.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The evaluator cannot verify that the project was generated specifically from webext.eu (vs. manually creating files). This is an inherent limitation of file-based state verification, but acceptable given that webext.eu always generates manifest.json and any valid completion would produce this file.
